questions.title: Does the manual state these troubleshooting facts?

source.text: PROBLEM (same as row above): Pump fails to operate. | CAUSE: Obstructed fluid hose or gun/valve; fluid hose ID is too small. | SOLUTION: Clear*; use a hose with a larger ID.

PROBLEM (same as row above): Pump operates, but output is low on both strokes. | CAUSE: Obstructed fluid hose or gun/valve; fluid hose ID is too small. | SOLUTION: Clear*; use a hose with a larger ID.

* To determine if the fluid hose or gun is obstructed, follow the Pressure Relief Procedure on page 8. Disconnect the fluid hose and place a container at the pump fluid outlet to catch any fluid. Turn on the air just enough to start the pump (about 20–40 psi [0.14–0.3 MPa, 1.4–2.8 bar]). If the pump starts when the air is turned on, the obstruc- tion is in the fluid hose or gun.

proposal: 1. Meaning: For this problem or cause the manual prescribes this check or test (it need not repair anything). Conditions: Turn on air just enough to start the pump; about 20–40 psi [0.14–0.3 MPa, 1.4–2.8 bar].

3. FailureMode 'Obstructed fluid hose or gun/valve; fluid hose ID too small' -> RESOLVED_BY -> CorrectiveAction 'Check whether the pump starts when the air is turned on' [inspection]. Meaning: For this problem or cause the manual prescribes this check or test (it need not repair anything). Conditions: If the pump starts when the air is turned on, the obstruction is in the fluid hose or gun.

answers.rationale: The footnote prescribes disconnecting the hose and placing a container, applying about 20–40 psi air, and checking whether the pump starts to determine whether the fluid hose or gun is obstructed, matching all three inspection statements.

answers.text: The listed solution is “Clear*; see Technical Data on pages 24–27”; the excerpt does not prescribe consulting the Technical Data as an inspection or test.
answers.rationale: The manual lists clearing as the solution and merely refers to the Technical Data, so it does not support the proposed inspection action.

answers.text: The prescribed test checks whether the fluid hose or gun is obstructed; it does not check whether the hose ID is too small.
answers.rationale: The manual prescribes the obstruction test for the obstruction cause, but the proposed failure mode also includes a too-small hose ID, which that test does not assess.
The row prescribes cleaning and refers to the Service pages; it does not prescribe consulting those pages as a check or test.
